flagged.title: Acts 1-2: The Merry War & Deceptions
flagged.reason: The video incorrectly defines and identifies Beatrice's rhymed soliloquy as unrhymed blank verse, which is a technical form error that would penalize a GCSE student on AO2.

mark_affecting.quote: She speaks in blank verse... shifting into blank verse is basically a giant neon sign signaling emotional sincerity

flagged.title: Acts 4-5: Truth & Resolution
flagged.reason: Slide 4 explicitly highlights and misattributes the Act 4 Scene 1 romantic confession 'none left to protest' as an Act 5 denial of love, which would penalise a student quoting it in an exam.

mark_affecting.quote: They deny their love saying none left to protest, but give in when their love poems to each other are produced.

flagged.title: Language & Structure
flagged.reason: The video quotes an invented Shakespeare line ('I would my horse had the speed of your departure') and swaps the speakers of the actual line, which would penalise a GCSE English Literature student citing textual evidence.

mark_affecting.quote: Beatrice lobs an insult, saying she wishes her horse had the speed of his tongue, and Benedick immediately smashes it right back: 'I would my horse had the speed of your departure.'
